1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely from the server-side session via owner()/verified() with no client-supplied user identifiers, and all POSTs enforce a CSRF token check.

2.why: Identity challenges are bound to the requesting session and TOTP/recovery secrets to the single account record, so a code issued for one context cannot validate for another user (and only one account exists).

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/authenticator/confirm only sets mfa=true and never revokes other existing sessions, so prior sessions for the account remain usable (rotation happens only at login).

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted and recovery codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes; neither is persisted in plaintext.

5.why: All secrets, OTPs, recovery codes, session IDs, and nonces are generated from crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and the client keeps the CSRF token and codes only in memory variables, with no localStorage/sessionStorage or readable cookies.

7.why: The server validates email format/length, password length, 6-digit codes via six(), and recovery format via rec(), and there is no SQL/database layer to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted into the DOM via textContent and the CSP requires script/style nonces, so injected markup or script cannot execute.

9.why: The application issues no HTTP redirects at all (no Location logic) and client navigation is internal view switching, so redirects cannot be abused to leave the app.

10.why: Responses set HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', plus Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control: no-store, and Permissions-Policy.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets the mfa_session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Although the server never logs secrets and returns generic errors without stack traces, the client deliberately writes the TOTP seed, identity OTP, and backup codes to the browser console and a persistent on-page 'Logs' panel, so they are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Identity codes carry used/expires flags (10-minute life), TOTP confirmation records accepted counters to block reuse, and recovery codes are deleted upon use with a one-year expiry.

14.why: Login, identity, authenticator, and recovery verification each track failures and impose a 5-minute lockout with HTTP 429 after 5 failed attempts.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID (rotation), current() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
